a chemical element; here, the gases (CO2) that harm the climate

having decided strongly to do something

vocabulary.meaning_en: the soft part inside your mouth used for tasting and speaking
vocabulary.example: Don't burn your tongue on the hot soup.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the short thick finger on your hand
tired and unhappy because nothing interesting is happening

fine_lines.title: Carbon footprint vs plastic footprint
fine_lines.explanation_ar: carbon footprint كمية الغازات الضارة (مثل ثاني أكسيد الكربون) التي تنتج عن نشاطك، كالسفر بالطائرة أو القيادة. plastic footprint كمية البلاستيك التي تستعملها وترميها.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Your carbon footprint is the amount of harmful gas (CO2) your activities produce, e.g. flying or driving. Your plastic footprint is the amount of plastic you use and throw away.

examples.sentence: Taking the train instead of flying lowers your carbon footprint.
Using a refillable bottle reduces your plastic footprint.

fine_lines.title: Bite your tongue vs twiddle your thumbs
fine_lines.explanation_ar: bite your tongue أن تمنع نفسك من قول شيء تريد قوله. twiddle your thumbs أن تبقى بلا عمل وتنتظر بملل.
fine_lines.explanation_en: 'Bite your tongue' = stop yourself from saying something. 'Twiddle your thumbs' = wait and do nothing because you have nothing to do.

examples.sentence: I wanted to argue, but I bit my tongue.
The internet was down, so we just twiddled our thumbs.

expressions.meaning_en: (1) turning over completely, e.g. when falling; (2) completely and very much
expressions.example: He tripped on the step and fell head over heels.

expressions.meaning_en: the amount of plastic a person or company uses and throws away
expressions.example: Our school is trying to reduce its plastic footprint.

expressions.meaning_en: a serious, determined expression before a competition or challenge
expressions.example: Before the final, she put her game face on.

expressions.meaning_en: to stop yourself from saying what you think
expressions.example: I wanted to complain about the food, but I bit my tongue.

expressions.meaning_en: to wait with nothing to do
expressions.example: The meeting started late, so we sat twiddling our thumbs.

expressions.meaning_en: the amount of carbon dioxide your activities put into the air
expressions.example: Cycling to work helps cut my carbon footprint.

expressions.meaning_en: to look at something with great pleasure
expressions.example: Feast your eyes on this beautiful view!

expressions.meaning_en: to be something someone can't stop thinking about
expressions.example: That silly mistake I made in the exam lives rent-free in my head.

grammar.title: Changing the pronoun in body idioms
grammar.explanation_ar: في تعابير الجسم نغيّر كلمة الملكية حسب الفاعل: I bit my tongue، she bit her tongue، they twiddled their thumbs. والفعل bite ماضيه bit.
grammar.explanation_en: In body idioms, change the possessive to match the subject: I bit my tongue, she bit her tongue, they twiddled their thumbs. Note: bite → bit (past).
examples: He put his game face on.
That joke lives rent-free in my head.
